result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn rent into an index and plot it next to the regional price index, so neither shows raw dollars alone. Neither states the inflation-adjusted rise of about 12% or offers a series in 2016 dollars, but B at least spells out the gap (rent grew about 15 percentage points faster than prices). B also has a finding-style title and labels its lines directly, while A uses a question as its title and adds a separate legend. Both y-axes start at 100 without explaining why. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers index rent and the price index to 2016 = 100 and plot them as two lines. That makes the gap visible, but neither shows rent in 2016 dollars or says the real increase is about 12%. A puts labels right at the line ends, including the dollar change ($1,180 → $1,745), states the 15-point gap, and has a flyer-ready title that states the finding. B's title is only a question, it repeats its direct labels in a detached legend, and it leans on a long table, so A is better.
